ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CDB$, $\angle ACB=\angle CDB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC$, $CD=BD$. Connect $AD$ and intersect $BC$ at point $P$. What is the value of $\tan\angle CAP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ACB=\angle CDB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$, $CD=BD$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ACB$ and $\triangle CDB$ are isosceles right triangles,\\
therefore $\angle ABC+\angle CBD=90^\circ$\\
thus $\angle ABD+\angle CDB=180^\circ$\\
which means $CD\parallel AB$\\
hence $\triangle CDP\sim \triangle BAP$,\\
let $CD=DB=a$, then $CB=\sqrt{2}a$, $AB=2a$\\
therefore, $\frac{CD}{AB}=\frac{CP}{BP}=\frac{1}{2}$\\
thus, $\frac{CP}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$\\
Since $AC=BC$\\
it follows that $\tan\angle CAP=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$

method.method_draft: Synthetic similarity route. First read the diagram: points C, P, B are collinear, A, P, D are collinear, and P is the intersection of AD with BC; A and D lie on opposite sides of line BC as drawn. From the text, triangle ABC is right isosceles at C, so angle ABC = 45 degrees, and triangle CDB is right isosceles at D, so angle CBD = 45 degrees. Using the visual order around B, angle ABD = angle ABC + angle CBD = 90 degrees. Since angle CDB is also 90 degrees, AB is parallel to CD. Then with AD and BC as transversals, triangles BAP and CDP are similar. Let CD = BD = a. Then CB = sqrt(2)a, and because AC = BC, AB = 2a. Hence CD/AB = 1/2, so CP/BP = 1/2. Therefore CP/BC = 1/3. Finally, since P lies on BC and AC is perpendicular to BC, triangle ACP is right at C, so tan angle CAP = CP/AC = CP/BC = 1/3.

再推理：按坐标法处理。因为所求的 tan∠CAP 在旋转、平移、缩放下不变，取 BC 为基准，设 C=(0,0)，B=(1,0)。由 ∠ACB=90° 且 AC=BC，令 A=(0,1)。设 D=(x,y)。由 CD=BD 得 x^2+y^2=(x-1)^2+y^2，所以 x=1/2。又 ∠CDB=90°，则向量 C-D 与 B-D 垂直，即 x(x-1)+y^2=0。代入 x=1/2，得 y^2=1/4。图中 D 与 A 在 BC 两侧，而 A 的 y 坐标为正，所以 D=(1/2,-1/2)。直线 AD 过 A(0,1) 和 D(1/2,-1/2)，斜率为 (-1/2-1)/(1/2-0)=-3，因此方程为 y=1-3x。与 BC 即 y=0 相交时，x=1/3，所以 P=(1/3,0)。在直角三角形 ACP 中，AC=1，CP=1/3，因此 tan∠CAP=CP/AC=1/3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CDB$, $\angle ACB=\angle CDB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC$, $CD=BD$. Connect $AD$ and let it intersect $BC$ at point $P$. What is the value of $\tan\angle CAP$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Since $\angle ACB=\angle CDB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$, $CD=BD$, it follows that $\triangle ACB$ and $\triangle CDB$ are isosceles right triangles. Therefore $\angle ABC+\angle CBD=90^\circ$, thus $\angle ABD+\angle CDB=180^\circ$, which means $CD\parallel AB$. Hence $\triangle CDP\sim \triangle BAP$. Let $CD=DB=a$, then $CB=\sqrt{2}a$, $AB=2a$. Therefore, $\frac{CD}{AB}=\frac{CP}{BP}=\frac{1}{2}$, thus $\frac{CP}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$. Since $AC=BC$, it follows that $\tan\angle CAP=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$.

Image description: The attached figure is a geometric figure, with labeled point A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C above and slightly toward the middle, D at the upper right, and P in the middle of the figure; in the figure it can be seen that C, P, B are collinear, A, P, D are collinear, P is the intersection point of AD and BC, and A, D are located on two sides of line BC.
Reasoning: From the problem statement, ∠ACB=90° and AC=BC, so △ABC is an isosceles right triangle with C as the right-angle vertex, hence ∠ABC=45°. Also ∠CDB=90° and CD=BD, so △CDB is an isosceles right triangle with D as the right-angle vertex, hence ∠CBD=45°. According to the order of the rays at point B in the figure, ∠ABD=∠ABC+∠CBD=45°+45°=90°. Also ∠CDB=90°, so AB and CD are both perpendicular to BD, and thus CD∥AB.
Since AD and BC are respectively transversals, and CD∥AB, △CDP∼△BAP. Let CD=BD=a, then in the isosceles right △CDB, CB=√2a. Also AC=BC=√2a, and in the isosceles right △ABC, AB=√2·AC=2a. Therefore CD/AB=a/(2a)=1/2. From similar triangles, CP/BP=CD/AB=1/2, so if CP=x, then BP=2x, BC=3x, hence CP/BC=1/3. Because P is on BC, and AC⊥BC, △ACP is right-angled at C, tan∠CAP=CP/AC. Also AC=BC, therefore tan∠CAP=CP/BC=1/3.
